subject.title: [Feature]: WebUI notification system, cron job management popups, and context monitor integration

question: Should OpenClaw add a core connected-Control-UI in-app notification/action queue for cron results and context pressure, and which related action surfaces should share that contract?
rationale: Current main has several partial notification, cron, and context surfaces, while the remaining request changes Control UI product architecture and overlaps related open notification/action issues rather than being a narrow bug repair.

options.title: Scope Shared Queue First
options.body: Define one connected-Control-UI notification/action contract and then wire cron-finished and context-pressure events into it in focused follow-up work.

options.title: Fold Into Related Action Issues
options.body: Make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/53228 or https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/46656 the canonical shared action/notification API work and use this issue as UX requirements.

options.title: Defer Broad Toasts
options.body: Keep the current inline cron, Web Push, and context-ring surfaces only, and close this later if maintainers reject a core toast/snooze layer.

recommendation.title: Scope Shared Queue First
recommendation.body: Define one connected-Control-UI notification/action contract and then wire cron-finished and context-pressure events into it in focused follow-up work.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining product boundary touches cron notification routing history and prior review comments on this issue.
